true_answer: For a given predicate P ( x ) , you might believe that the statements ∀ xP ( x ) or ∃ xP ( x ) are either true or false. How would you decide if you were correct in each case? You have four choices: you could give an example of an element n in the domain for which P ( n ) is true or for which P ( n ) if false, or you could argue that no matter what n is, P ( n ) is true or is false. (a) What would you need to do to prove ∀ xP ( x ) is true? (b) What would you need to do to prove ∀ xP ( x ) is false? (c) What would you need to do to prove ∃ xP ( x ) is true?
